name: Practice (abhyāsa)
method_summary: The effort toward stability of the mind (YS 1.13): the carrying out of the means to the peaceful flow of a mind without activities, from the wish to accomplish it, with endeavour, vigour and enthusiasm (YBh 1.13). It becomes firmly grounded when followed for a long time, without a break, and with earnestness (satkāra), accomplished through austerity, continence/studentship, knowledge and faith (YS 1.14, YBh 1.14).
signs_of_progress: Firmly grounded practice is 'not suddenly overcome by the impression of emergence' (YBh 1.14).

name: Dispassion (vairāgya)
method_summary: Lower: the consciousness of mastery (vaśīkāra-saṃjñā) of one free of thirst for seen and scripture-taught objects; by the power of discerning insight the mind sees the faults of objects, and has a consciousness of mastery without engagement and empty of rejecting and taking (YS 1.15, YBh 1.15). Higher: freedom from thirst for the guṇas themselves, from knowing the puruṣa (YS 1.16); Vyāsa: 'only the clearness of knowledge', of which kaivalya is inseparable (YBh 1.16). Dispassion makes the stream toward objects barren (YBh 1.12).
signs_of_progress: The yogin's own thought at the higher dispassion: 'What was to be attained is attained; the afflictions to be destroyed are destroyed; the linked chain of becoming is cut' (YBh 1.16).

name: Practice on a single principle (ekatattva-abhyāsa)
method_summary: To remove the distractions, the mind is practised with a single principle as its support (YS 1.32, YBh 1.32). Vyāsa argues that the mind is one and has many objects and abides, not merely momentary cognitions each fixed to one object.

name: Cultivating the four attitudes (maitrī, karuṇā, muditā, upekṣā)
method_summary: By cultivating friendliness toward the happy, compassion toward the suffering, gladness toward the virtuous and equanimity toward the non-virtuous, the mind becomes clear (YS 1.33). Vyāsa: from such cultivation a pure (śukla) dharma arises; from that the mind becomes clear; the clear mind, one-pointed, gains a footing of stability (YBh 1.33).
signs_of_progress: Clarity of mind (citta-prasādana), then one-pointed stability (YBh 1.33).

name: Devotion to Īśvara (īśvara-praṇidhāna)
method_summary: Devotion, a special kind of bhakti, by which Īśvara favours the yogin by mere intent thought (YS 1.23, YBh 1.23); in kriyā-yoga it is the offering of all actions to the supreme teacher or the renouncing of their fruit (YBh 2.1, 2.32). Through it the obstacles do not arise and the yogin sees his own form (YS 1.29); it brings the perfection of samādhi (YS 2.45).
signs_of_progress: The obstacles do not arise; sight of one's own form (YBh 1.29); perfection of samādhi (YS 2.45).

name: Repetition of and meditation on Oṃ (praṇava-japa)
method_summary: Repetition of the praṇava and contemplation of the meaning it denotes, Īśvara; the mind becomes one-pointed (YS 1.27–1.28, YBh 1.28). Vyāsa quotes: from self-study take up yoga, from yoga bring self-study to mind; by their perfection the supreme self shines.

name: Kriyā-yoga (austerity, self-study, devotion to Īśvara)
method_summary: Austerity (tapas), self-study (svādhyāya) and devotion to Īśvara (YS 2.1): for the practitioner whose mind is not yet concentrated. Practised, it brings samādhi into being and thins the afflictions, making them like burnt seeds (YS 2.2, YBh 2.2).

warnings.text: tac ca cittaprasādanam abādhamānam anenāsevyam iti manyate
warnings.gloss: Vyāsa: that austerity is to be practised by him without harming the clarity of the mind.

name: Austerity (tapas)
method_summary: In kriyā-yoga and as an observance (niyama): the means without which the impurity variegated by karma, afflictions and tendencies cannot be broken up (YBh 2.1). Vyāsa: bearing the pairs of opposites — hunger and thirst, cold and heat, standing and sitting, silence of wood and of gesture; he names vows (kṛcchra, cāndrāyaṇa, sāṃtapana and the like) without describing them (YBh 2.32). It destroys impurity and the covering, and perfection of body and senses follows (YS 2.43). Fasting-type vows are named only; no method is recorded here.

warnings.text: tac ca cittaprasādanam abādhamānam anenāsevyam iti manyate
warnings.gloss: Vyāsa: it is to be practised without harming the clarity of the mind (citta-prasādana).

name: Self-study (svādhyāya)
method_summary: Study of the scriptures of liberation or repetition of the praṇava and the other purifying syllables (YBh 2.1, 2.32); from it, union with the chosen deity (YS 2.44), and gods, sages and perfected ones come into view (YBh 2.44).

name: Cultivating the opposite (pratipakṣa-bhāvanā)
method_summary: When harmful thoughts oppress, one cultivates their opposites (YS 2.33): Vyāsa gives the thought 'I took refuge in the dharma of yoga by giving safety to all beings; taking the harmful thoughts up again I am like a dog licking its vomit' (YBh 2.33), and contemplates the unwanted ripening that follows harmful thoughts — unending suffering and ignorance (YS 2.34, YBh 2.34). Also the way the afflictions are thinned (YBh 2.4).

warnings.text: evaṃ vitarkāṇāṃ cāmum evānugataṃ vipākam aniṣṭaṃ bhāvayan na vitarkeṣu manaḥ praṇidadhīta
warnings.gloss: Vyāsa: contemplating the unwanted ripening that follows harmful thoughts, one should not set the mind on them.

name: The restraints (yama)
method_summary: Non-harming, truthfulness, non-stealing, continence, non-possessiveness (YS 2.30); not limited by birth, place, time or occasion, they are the great vow (YS 2.31). Vyāsa: the others are rooted in non-harming and taught to make it pure (YBh 2.30).
signs_of_progress: Signs of establishment: hostility abandoned in one's presence; actions and fruits rest on one; jewels present themselves; vigour is gained; understanding of the how of births (YS 2.35–2.39).

name: Non-harming (ahiṃsā)
method_summary: Absence of hostility toward all beings, in every way and at all times (YBh 2.30); the root of the other restraints. Limits by class, place, time or occasion (a fisherman harming only fish; 'not at a holy place'; 'not on holy days'; 'only for a god or a Brāhmaṇa', or warriors in battle) are shown by Vyāsa as what the great vow does not have (YBh 2.31).
signs_of_progress: Hostility is abandoned in the presence of one established in it (YS 2.35).

name: Truthfulness (satya)
method_summary: Speech and mind in accord with the fact, as seen and as inferred, spoken to pass on one's understanding without deceit or error and for the benefit of all beings (YBh 2.30).
signs_of_progress: One established in it: actions and their fruits rest on him (YS 2.36).

warnings.text: yadi caivam apy abhidhīyamānā bhūtopaghātaparaiva syān na satyaṃ bhavet pāpam eva bhavet tena puṇyābhāsena puṇyapratirūpakeṇa kaṣṭaṃ tamaḥ prāpnuyāt
warnings.gloss: Vyāsa: if speech, even so uttered, only harms beings, it is not truth but sin, and one reaches grievous darkness through a mere semblance of merit.
Vyāsa: therefore, after examining, one should speak the truth that is for the good of all beings.

name: Non-stealing (asteya)
method_summary: Absence of longing (aspṛhā) for others' goods; stealing is taking goods contrary to scripture (YBh 2.30).

name: Continence (brahmacarya)
method_summary: Restraint of the generative organ in one whose senses are guarded (YBh 2.30). Restricted-adjacent (sexual topic): only the definition is recorded.

name: Non-possessiveness (aparigraha)
method_summary: Non-acceptance of objects on seeing the faults of acquiring, keeping, losing, attachment and harming in them (YBh 2.30).
signs_of_progress: Understanding of the how of births (YS 2.39).

name: The observances (niyama)
method_summary: Purity, contentment, austerity, self-study and devotion to Īśvara (YS 2.32).
signs_of_progress: Disgust for one's own body and non-contact with others; purity of sattva, cheerfulness, one-pointedness, mastery of the senses, fitness for seeing the self; unsurpassed happiness; perfection of body and senses; union with the chosen deity; perfection of samādhi (YS 2.40–2.45).

name: Purity (śauca)
method_summary: Outer: by earth, water and the like, and eating what is clean; inner: washing away the taints of the mind (YBh 2.32). Result: disgust for one's own body and non-contact with others (YS 2.40); purity of sattva, cheerfulness, one-pointedness, mastery of the senses and fitness for seeing the self (YS 2.41).

name: Contentment (saṃtoṣa)
method_summary: Not wishing to take more than the means at hand (YBh 2.32). Result: unsurpassed happiness (YS 2.42).

name: Posture (āsana)
method_summary: Steady and comfortable (YS 2.46); accomplished by relaxing effort and by coalescence with the endless (YS 2.47); from it, no assault by the pairs of opposites (YS 2.48). Vyāsa lists names of postures only (lotus, auspicious, svastika, staff, supported, couch, curlew, elephant, camel, even configuration, steady-comfortable, as-comfortable); no method is given.
signs_of_progress: No shaking of the limbs (YBh 2.47); not overcome by cold and heat and the like (YBh 2.48).

name: Breath-regulation (prāṇāyāma) in the Yoga Sūtra
method_summary: Restricted-adjacent (breath retention): summary only. Defined as the cutting off of the course of inhalation and exhalation once posture is mastered (YS 2.49); Vyāsa names external, internal and suspended forms, regulated by place, time and number (YS 2.50), and a fourth that goes beyond the external and internal (YS 2.51); no figures or steps are recorded here. Result: the covering of the light dwindles and the mind becomes fit for concentration (YS 2.52–2.53).
signs_of_progress: The covering of the light dwindles moment by moment (YBh 2.52).

name: The fourth prāṇāyāma (YS 2.51)
method_summary: Restricted-adjacent (breath retention): summary only. Vyāsa: the fourth goes beyond both the external and the internal; unlike the third, which is a single-effort stopping without attention to an object, it is a gradual stopping preceded by surpassing both, by mastery of the ground, after determining the object of inhalation and exhalation.

name: Expulsion and retention of breath (YS 1.34)
method_summary: Restricted-adjacent (breath retention): summary only. The sūtra offers expulsion and retention of the breath as one means to steadiness of mind; Vyāsa only glosses expulsion as expulsion of the belly-air through the nostrils by a special effort and retention as prāṇāyāma (YBh 1.34); Vyāsa relates it to fitness for concentration (YBh 2.53). No method, count or duration is recorded.

name: Sense-withdrawal (pratyāhāra) in the Yoga Sūtra
method_summary: The senses' seeming imitation of the mind's own form when not in contact with their own objects (YS 2.54). Vyāsa: when the mind is stilled the senses are stilled like it, needing no other means, as bees follow the queen bee (YBh 2.54); from it, supreme mastery of the senses (YS 2.55), of which Vyāsa gives four views (YBh 2.55).

name: The eight limbs of yoga as a practice (yogāṅga-anuṣṭhāna)
method_summary: The practice of the eight limbs (YS 2.29) destroys impurity, and the light of knowledge rises up to discriminative discernment (YS 2.28); it is the cause of separation from impurity and of attaining discernment (YBh 2.28).

name: Cultivating discriminative discernment (viveka-khyāti)
method_summary: The cognition of the difference between sattva and puruṣa; unwavering (aviplava) discernment is the means of abandonment (YS 2.26). While false knowledge has not ceased it 'floats'; when false knowledge has come to the burnt-seed state, the stream of discerning cognition becomes stainless (YBh 2.26).

name: Concentration giving rise to subtle sense-perception (YS 1.35)
method_summary: Holding the mind at the tip of the nose, tip of tongue, palate, middle of tongue or root of tongue gives awareness of divine smell, taste, form, touch or sound; such activities bind the mind to steadiness and dispel doubt; purpose: to confirm scripture, inference and teacher by some one directly known thing (YBh 1.35).

name: The sorrowless, luminous activity (YS 1.36)
method_summary: Holding the mind at the lotus of the heart gives awareness of the buddhi, like the light of the sun, moon, planet or jewel; the mind in I-am-ness alone becomes like a waveless ocean (YBh 1.36).

name: Mind on one free of passion (YS 1.37)
method_summary: The mind coloured by the mind of one free of passion as its support gains a footing of steadiness (YBh 1.37).

name: Support in the knowledge of dream and sleep (YS 1.38)
method_summary: The mind taking on the form of the knowledge of dream or sleep as its support gains a footing of steadiness (YBh 1.38).

name: Meditation on whatever is agreeable (YS 1.39)
method_summary: One meditates on just what is agreeable; the mind that has gained steadiness there gains it in other objects too (YBh 1.39).

name: Meditation (dhyāna) as the means of abandoning the afflictions' activities
method_summary: The gross activities of the afflictions, thinned by kriyā-yoga, are abandoned by meditation as discerning insight (prasaṃkhyāna), until they are subtle, like burnt seeds (YS 2.11, YBh 2.11).
